## Who answered

Describe the achieved sample here: who it represents, who is missing, and
anything that skews it (a young panel, one dominant region, ...).

```{python}
ez.calc_percentage(d, "demo_gender", sort="desc").pipe(ez.plot_bars)
```

```{python}
ez.calc_percentage(d, "demo_edu", sort="asc").pipe(ez.plot_bars, flip=True)
```

```{python}
ez.calc_percentage_multi(d, "motivations_", id="respondent_id", sort="asc").pipe(
    ez.plot_bars, label="option", flip=True
)
```

## Satisfaction and NPS

State the score, how it compares to whatever benchmark you have (last wave,
sector norm), and where the promoters and detractors sit.

```{python}
ez.plot_nps_gauge(ez.calc_nps(d, "nps_value")["nps"].iloc[0])
```

```{python}
ez.plot_nps(d, "nps_value")
```

## What drives satisfaction

Read the matrix by quadrant: top-left (important, delivered poorly) is the
to-do list; top-right (important, delivered well) is what to protect.

```{python}
ez.ipm_model(d, "nps_value", "ratings_").pipe(ez.plot_ipm)
```
